title: Winch Recovery Cable Tensile Failure: Forensic Metallurgical Inquest
description: Upper-intermediate engineering module investigating winch recovery cable tensile failure: forensic metallurgical inquest.
learning_objectives: Master professional Causative Verbs & Passive Reporting in automotive engineering
Eliminate common Czech interference errors in winch recovery cable tensile failure: forensic metallurgical inquest
Demonstrate precision in technical and regulatory documentation

questions.prompt: _____ earlier during simulation, the catastrophic torsional stress on the central backbone tube would not have occurred on the test track.

explanations.correct: Inverted Third Conditional 'had the engineers increased' correctly replaces 'If [subject] had...' in formal engineering inquests.
explanations.wrong_A: 'if engineers increased' lacks auxiliary 'had' and creates an incomplete clause.
explanations.wrong_C: 'would engineers have increased' incorrectly places 'would have' inside the conditional premise.
explanations.wrong_D: 'should engineers increase' expresses present/future tentative condition, not a past counterfactual.

questions.cz_learning_point: Formal engineering reports invert past conditionals without 'if': 'Had the engineers increased...' = 'If the engineers had increased...'. Never put 'would' into the condition.
